summary: Candidate B passes the bounded design review. No mandatory contradiction, unsafe asserted trust assumption, omitted foundation criterion or unauthorized source expansion was found. This pass establishes design eligibility only; implementation, actual native behavior and enforced isolation remain unverified.

task_snapshot.purpose: Assignment and registration observation only; later unrelated Task revisions do not change the frozen baseline.

recorded_confirmation.evidence: Actual native reviewer confirmed complete SOUL and role reads with corrected transcription matching exact canonical role digests.

criteria.criterion: Neutral starter has no live identity/branch set, standing grant, schedule or autonomous-write permission.
criteria.assessment: The starter is explicitly unselected: identities, branches, schedules, budgets, entitlements and autonomous writes do not become active defaults.

criteria.criterion: Missing, malformed, expired or incompatible selections produce precise unavailable/blocked diagnostics.
criteria.assessment: Strict parsing and select_operation return exact missing, malformed, expired, incompatible and unavailable conditions without status side effects.

criteria.criterion: Project specialization is capability-only; standing entitlements remain absent until deliberately accepted at adoption.
criteria.assessment: Capability specialization is descriptive; only a previously accepted protected issuer record can create standing authority.

criteria.criterion: AGENTS.md, README sections, generated wiki and Task responses have distinct owners and update routes.
criteria.assessment: AGENTS governance, scoped factual README sections, generated wiki sources and append-only Task history use distinct routes.

criteria.criterion: Overrides, generators, stable identities and protected sections resolve conservatively; unknown/mixed targets hold unsafe edits.
criteria.assessment: Source-bound sections, an immutable protected minimum, conservative override precedence, stable identity and mixed/unknown holds satisfy the classification design.

criteria.criterion: Grants bind actor/project/branch/policy/source/payload/scope/owner and freshness; valid standing entitlements avoid redundant approval.
criteria.assessment: The exact grant binds native identity, project/branch, current policy and classification, source/payload, scope/budget, current owner and freshness. Accepted standing entitlements can mint fresh grants without another approval.

criteria.criterion: Candidate-controlled code and environment cannot alter broker policy, credentials or effective approval logic.
criteria.assessment: The broker owns transport, uses closed requests and frozen owner imports, clean environment and pinned executables. Confinement and import-injection proofs remain required.

criteria.criterion: Broker routes canonical mutations to their existing helper owners and rejects arbitrary shell instructions.
criteria.assessment: Typed dispatch retains the Task closed event union and existing memory/ontology publishers and journals. Arbitrary shell/protocol forwarding is explicitly excluded.

criteria.criterion: Caller identity comes from the trusted native request envelope and current manager binding, not an actor string in model arguments; workers cannot read private grants or broker credentials.
criteria.assessment: AuthenticatedCall is transport-created, correlated with an active native request and canonical assignment. Actor arguments are rejected; grants and credentials are excluded from candidate reads.

criteria.criterion: One controller/charter is selected per execution; reading a charter does not activate it.
criteria.assessment: Controller origin and charter are versioned execution facts. Explicit routing keeps Director default and charter reading cannot activate a controller.

criteria.criterion: Specialist responsibilities, qualifications, role reads, scope and stopping rules are explicit; generic Director use and category rules are preserved.
criteria.assessment: Narrow specialist duties, exact role pairs, fresh catalog/fit checks, separate skills/tools checks and unchanged category topology are explicit.

criteria.criterion: New provenance is schema-versioned and validated; historical records retain bytes/meaning and unknown fields are rejected.
criteria.assessment: Task schema 2 receives orchestration version 2; native observations and grants dispatch explicitly. Historical Task/record/config/grant semantics and strict unknown-field rejection are retained.

criteria.criterion: Curator bootstrap reserves exactly one manager, activates only the real receipt identity and relinquishes canonical Task writing.
criteria.assessment: Reservation precedes launch; actual native lineage and role/charter acknowledgement gate activation. The controller relinquishes the sole Task writer role.

criteria.criterion: Existing record/configuration schemas keep their meaning; any changed grant envelope has explicit version dispatch.
criteria.assessment: Memory grant 2 and ontology grant 3 extend native provenance; ontology core/advanced profiles preserve their distinct prior guards. Record/config schemas and old grant paths keep their meaning.

criteria.criterion: Only the current confirmed manager with exact operation scope can publish Curator knowledge; ordinary workers and forged provenance fail.
criteria.assessment: Publication compares the transport caller with current Task writer/execution/generation, activation, exact source/config/proposal and separate owner grant/scope; ordinary workers remain proposal-only.

criteria.criterion: Activation, manager/child discovery, supervision, interrupt and resume observations are mapped without forging collaboration receipts.
criteria.assessment: The adapter preserves real App Server IDs and current observations, rejects forged legacy receipts and uses version-pinned control mappings. Missing complete protocol support blocks the affected path.

criteria.criterion: Effective model/effort and independent contexts are checked; missing capabilities hold work.
criteria.assessment: Requested settings are distinguished from effective settings; null effort and unverified inheritance block dispatch. Identical frozen solver inputs and sibling exclusion have separate proof obligations.

criteria.criterion: Real observations establish identities, reservation-before-launch, one canonical writer, full required teams, settings inheritance and isolated solver input.
criteria.assessment: The unchanged NP protocol requires actual controller/manager identities, reservation order, full disjoint teams, one writer, effective settings, isolated solver input and real owner publication. These observations are not claimed yet.

criteria.criterion: Capacity queuing preserves every required agent; uncertain or absent observations are named non-passes.
criteria.assessment: Capacity queues retain all distinct required agents. Missing, stale or uncertain observations do not establish stopping, publisher leases or successful completion.

criteria.criterion: Candidate writes to trusted policy/broker, canonical ledgers, control records, grants and credentials are denied by the enforced boundary.
criteria.assessment: The proposed enforced profile protects broker/policy/helper/grant/credential/canonical paths for actual candidates and descendants, with paired positive actions and actual denial plus unchanged canary inventories.

criteria.criterion: Malicious branch/diff/note/config, process execution and broker-request cases cannot gain authority or bypass publication.
criteria.assessment: Adversarial obligations cover malicious text, self-approval, impersonation/replay, direct execution, path aliases, import injection, egress, sibling access and uncertain recovery without substituting JSON rejection for OS denial.

focused_assessments.assessment: The explicit version split is compatible with the current strict owner entry points if implemented as specified. Current memory authorize requires grant 1; ontology authorize dispatches grant 1/2, advanced conditions and exact scope; Task orchestration validates version 1 and actual legacy receipts. Candidate lines 56-66 preserve those paths and introduce distinct Curator branches instead of relabeling App Server IDs or Curator origin. No alternative publisher or lifecycle journal is introduced.

The design does not equate a restricted shell or an authenticated dynamic tool with whole-runtime isolation. It holds support if built-in sibling/control-message access remains possible, denies raw client protocol execution, disables unselected connectors/external tools and requires actual descendant enforcement. Implementation proof must inventory every enabled native channel, including commandExecution, fileChange, dynamicToolCall, mcpToolCall, collabAgentToolCall, webSearch, imageView, imageGeneration and permission-escalation requests. The supplied schema contains these channels; no OS proof is inferred from a named profile.

Candidate lines 84-86 put shared immutable inputs and candidate output outside sibling read scopes, with authenticated assignment-gated artifact transfer. They also identify native control messages and inherited context as separate leakage channels. This is a sound fail-closed design obligation; whether the selected runtime can enforce it remains an actual proof gate.

Candidate lines 16,50 and 96 expressly freeze the entire dynamically loaded owner/guard closure and its path/environment resolution. Current memory_evidence.installed_helper, ontology_authority.read_task, orchestration_state.role and decorated Task/memory guards load project-installed helpers. The later manifest must bind these copies and imports in the disposable trusted layout; hashing only curator_broker.py would violate the candidate.

Requested child settings, nullable thread settings, stale thread history and last-known collab states are explicitly insufficient. The design requires effective equality or a verified runtime-specific inheritance guarantee, and publication requires a current transport-correlated native call plus the exact active manager and owner grant. These checks avoid treating model arguments or ordinary observation JSON as authentication.

The proposed 40 charged turns, 60 minutes and 250000 observed tokens are a request to prepare, not an enforceable grant already present. Candidate line 153 explicitly blocks launch if the token cap cannot be enforced and requires an explicit host-supported bound. Charged-turn accounting must include native descendants; post-turn usage alone cannot prove a hard token cap. The deadline must close admission and reconcile ongoing owners. This is a preserved prelaunch gate, not a runtime pass.

focused_assessments.topic: Disposable proof scope and publication grants
focused_assessments.assessment: This reviewer has only its review directory and no proof, publication or canonical-write scope. The current foundation baseline source/evidence inventory does not itself instantiate the candidate proposed foundation_implementer/native-proof directory or its synthetic manager assignment. The manager must later reserve the exact implementer path and operation scope, and create the synthetic project-local manager assignment with exact MEMORY/ONTOLOGY/control-record writes checked by their owners. Separate Task/memory/ontology grants must reference that synthetic project and its current writer; a proof directory under an implementer artifact path is not itself a knowledge publication grant. Candidate lines 145-159 already require the exact host-authorized request before model/network work, so this is an execution prerequisite rather than a design rejection.
